main.tf:
data "aws_ami" "amazon_linux_2023" { most_recent = true owners = ["amazon"] filter { name = "name" values = ["al2023-ami-*-x86_64"] } filter { name = "architecture" values = ["x86_64"] } filter { name = "state" values = ["available"] } } data "aws_subnet" "public" { id = "subnet-00260868f0fd32bcf" } data "aws_security_group" "webapp_sg" { id = "sg-073152a7f6ed0e3fb" } resource "aws_instance" "webapp_instance" { ami = data.aws_ami.amazon_linux_2023.id instance_type = "t3.micro" subnet_id = data.aws_subnet.public.id vpc_security_group_ids = [data.aws_security_group.webapp_sg.id] associate_public_ip_address = true # Replace the instance whenever user-data changes so the fix is applied user_data_replace_on_change = true user_data = <<-EOF #!/bin/bash set -euxo pipefail # ── 1. Install Apache (httpd) ────────────────────────────────────────────── dnf install -y httpd # ── 2. Configure httpd to listen on port 8080 instead of 80 ─────────────── # Remove any existing Listen directives from the main config and all conf.d # fragments, then add a single authoritative Listen 8080. sed -i 's/^\s*Listen\s\+80\b.*/Listen 8080/' /etc/httpd/conf/httpd.conf # Remove any stray "Listen 80" lines that might appear in conf.d find /etc/httpd/conf.d/ -name '*.conf' \ -exec sed -i '/^\s*Listen\s\+80\b/d' {} \; # ── 3. Create the hello-world page ──────────────────────────────────────── mkdir -p /var/www/html cat > /var/www/html/index.html <<'HTML' Hello

Hello from AWS Full Stack

HTML # ── 4. Enable and start httpd ───────────────────────────────────────────── systemctl enable httpd systemctl restart httpd # ── 5. Wait until Apache is actually serving on port 8080 ───────────────── for i in $(seq 1 30); do if curl -sf http://127.0.0.1:8080/ > /dev/null 2>&1; then echo "Apache is serving on port 8080 (attempt $i)" exit 0 fi echo "Waiting for Apache ... attempt $i" sleep 2 done echo "ERROR: Apache did not come up on port 8080 within 60 s" >&2 exit 1 EOF tags = { Name = "webapp-instance" Stack = "instance" } }
